title: Bekhorot 48
description: Twins and intermingled newborns whose firstborn cannot be identified: when the priest receives five sela, ten or nothing, what happens if a child dies or the father dies, and Rava’s reading of the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda through Rav Asi’s brothers who are “half heirs, half purchasers” and Rav Pappa’s oral loan.

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְּרָה אִשְׁתּוֹ וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים לְכֹהֵן. מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — הָאָב פָּטוּר.

a2.he: מֵת הָאָב וְהַבָּנִים קַיָּימִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם נָתְנוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ — נָתָנוּ, וְאִם לָאו — פְּטוּרִין. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ דְּמִית הָאָב אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא דְּמִית לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — בְּהָא אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר כִּי חָלְקוּ פְּטוּרִין? וְהָא אִשְׁתַּעְבַּדוּ לְהוּ (לנכסי) [נִכְסֵי]!

a4.he: אֶלָּא, דְּמִית בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, מַאי שְׁנָא כִּי חָלְקוּ — דְּאָזֵיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וּמְדַחֵי לֵיהּ, דְּאָזֵיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וּמְדַחֵי לֵיהּ; כִּי לֹא חָלְקוּ נָמֵי — לֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידַחֲיֵיהּ, וְלֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידַחֲיֵיהּ!

a5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ בְּעִיר אַחַת, וְלָקְחוּ שָׂדֶה בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת — בַּעַל חוֹב גּוֹבֶה אוֹתָהּ מֵהֶם, דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בְּדִידָךְ מַסֵּיקְנָא — מְנָתָא דִּידָךְ קָא שָׁקֵילְנָא, וְאִי בְּחַבְרָךְ מַסֵּיקְנָא — מְנָתָא דְּחַבְרָךְ קָא שָׁקֵילְנָא.

a6.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי נִכְסֵי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ, מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּלְדִידֵיהּ לָא מָצֵי תָּבַע לֵיהּ, וּלְעָרֵב מָצֵי תָּבַע לֵיהּ? וְהָתְנַן: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב — לֹא יִפָּרַע מִן הֶעָרֵב, וְקַיְימָא לַן דְּלֹא יִתְבַּע מִן הֶעָרֵב תְּחִלָּה!

a7.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁמֵּת לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְאִי דְּאִיכָּא נִכְסֵי טוּבָא — הָכִי נָמֵי דְּשָׁקֵיל, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים.

a8.he: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב אַסִּי, דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ — מֶחֱצָה יוֹרְשִׁין וּמֶחֱצָה לָקוֹחוֹת, וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִלְוֶה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה

b1.he: לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, דְּאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַלָּקוֹחוֹת.

b2.he: וְהָכָא בְּחָמֵשׁ וְלֹא בַּחֲצִי חָמֵשׁ קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: חָמֵשׁ וַאֲפִילּוּ חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ.

b3.he: אִי הָכִי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים, נִתְחַיֵּיב גַּבְרָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! וְעוֹד, תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ, אִם יֵשׁ עֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה וַעֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה — חַיָּיבִין, וְאִם לָאו — פְּטוּרִין.

b4.he: מַאי עֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה וַעֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה? אִילֵּימָא בֵּין דִּירוּשָּׁה בֵּין דְּלָקוֹחוֹת, וְחָמֵשׁ וַאֲפִילּוּ חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ — אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא עֲשָׂרָה? אֲפִילּוּ בְּצִיר מֵעֲשָׂרָה נָמֵי!

b5.he: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא, עֲשָׂרָה זוּז דִּירוּשָּׁה לָזֶה, וַעֲשָׂרָה זוּז דִּירוּשָּׁה לָזֶה, אַלְמָא: חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!

b6.he: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ, וְהָכָא בִּדְרַב אַסִּי וְרַב פָּפָּא קָמִיפַּלְגִי.

b7.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ אַסֵּיפָא, נִתְחַיְּיבוּ הַנְּכָסִים, דְּמִית הָאָב אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא דְּמִית לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים, מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר כִּי חָלְקוּ פְּטוּרִין? הָא אִישְׁתַּעְבַּדוּ לְהוּ נִכְסֵי!

b8.he: אֶלָּא בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים, כִּי חָלְקוּ, אַמַּאי מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה? לֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי לִידַחֲיֵיהּ, וְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידְחֲיֵיהּ!

b9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ בְּעִיר אַחַת, וְלָקַח אֶחָד מֵהֶם שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ — בַּעַל חוֹב גּוֹבֶה מִמֶּנּוּ, דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בְּדִידָךְ מַסֵּיקְנָא — מְנָתָא דִּידָךְ קָא שָׁקֵילְנָא, וְאִי בְּחַבְרָךְ מַסֵּיקְנָא — מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדָא לִי מִקַּמֵּי דִּידָךְ.

b10.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי נִכְסוֹהִי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ, וְכוּלַּהּ כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא.

b11.he: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרוּ וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן עֲשָׂרָה סְלָעִים לַכֹּהֵן. מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, אִם לְכֹהֵן אֶחָד נָתַן — יַחֲזִיר לוֹ חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים, וְאִם לִשְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים נָתַן — אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָם.

b12.he: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה — נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים לַכֹּהֵן; שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b13.he: אַחַת בִּכֵּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרָה, וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים לַכֹּהֵן, מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — הָאָב פָּטוּר.

b14.he: מֵת הָאָב וְהַבָּנִים קַיָּימִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם נָתְנוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ נָתְנוּ, וְאִם לָאו פְּטוּרִין. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים, זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה אֵין לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b15.he: שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁל שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרוּ, וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — זֶה נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים לַכֹּהֵן וְזֶה נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים. מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים — אִם לַכֹּהֵן אֶחָד נָתָנוּ, יַחֲזִיר לָהֶם חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים. אִם לִשְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים נָתָנוּ — אֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָם.

b16.he: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — הָאָבוֹת פְּטוּרִין, וְהַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ; שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר, אוֹ שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וּשְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b17.he: אַחַת בִּכֵּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרָה, שֶׁל שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים, וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — זֶה שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְּרָה אִשְׁתּוֹ נוֹתֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים לַכֹּהֵן; זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

b18.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא שְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים, דְּאָזֵיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וּמְדַחֵי לֵיהּ, וְאָזֵיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וּמְדַחֵי לֵיהּ?

b19.he: כֹּהֵן אֶחָד נָמֵי לֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידַחֲיֵיהּ, וְלֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידַחֲיֵיהּ! אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:

messages.text: 47b closed with Rabbi Shimon on a child born by caesarean section and the son after him. Now a new mishna in chapter 8: births where it is not known which child opened the womb.
Mishna

With regard to one whose wife had not previously given birth and then gave birth to two males, i.e., twin males, and it is unknown which is the firstborn, he gives five sela coins to the priest after thirty days have passed.

notes.he: דאחד מהן בכור:
notes.en: Mishna. He gives five sela: since one of them is a firstborn.

messages.text: If one of them dies within thirty days of birth, before the obligation to redeem the firstborn takes effect, the father is exempt from the payment due to uncertainty, as perhaps it was the firstborn who died.

notes.he: דמצי למימר הבכור מת. וה"ה נמי לבן הנשאר דפטור והאי לישנא דנקט האב פטור משום סיפא דבעי למיתני מת האב כו':
notes.en: The father is exempt: since he can say, “The firstborn is the one who died.” The same applies to the remaining son: he too is exempt. The mishna words it “the father is exempt” because of the next clause, which goes on to teach “If the father died…”

notes.he: בתוך ל' יום האב פטור דמצי למימר הבכור מת:
notes.en: If one of them died within thirty days, the father is exempt: since he can say, “The firstborn is the one who died.”

messages.text: In a case where the father died and the sons are alive,

If they gave the five sela coins to the priest before they divided their father’s property between them, they gave it, and it remains in the possession of the priest. But if not, they are exempt from giving the redemption money to the priest.

notes.he: כדמפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Exempt: as the Gemara explains.

notes.he: דכל חד וחד מצי מדחי ליה:
notes.en: But if not, they are exempt: since each one of them can put him off.

messages.text: The obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property of the father; therefore, in either case the sons, his heirs, are required to pay the priest.

notes.he: בו נכסי האב לכהן כבעל חוב וחייבין לפרוע בין שניהם:
notes.en: The obligation took effect: the father’s property became obligated to the priest, as to a creditor, and the two of them together must pay.

notes.he: ולא מצו מדחו ליה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: the obligation took effect on the property, and they cannot put him off.

messages.text: If the wife gave birth to a male and a female and it is not known which was born first, the priest has nothing here, as it is possible that the female was born first.

notes.he: דאמר ליה הנקבה יצאת ראשון וכהן ידו על התחתונה דהמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: The priest has nothing here: since [the father] says to him, “The female came out first,” and the priest has the weaker hand, for the burden of proof rests on the one who would take from his fellow.

messages.text: Gemara

When did the father die? If we say that he died after the thirty days following the birth of his sons, does Rabbi Meir say in this case that if they divided their father’s property they are exempt from giving the redemption money to the priest? But the property is already on lien for the mitzva of redemption.
messages.quote: If they gave the five sela coins to the priest before they divided their father’s property … But if not, they are exempt

notes.he: דחוב מעליא הוא:
notes.en: Gemara. But the property is on lien: since it is a full debt.

notes.he: דקסבר השתא האחין שחלקו יורשין הן ומלוה על פה גובה מן היורשין אי נמי קסבר מלוה הכתובה בתורה ככתובה בשטר ומיהו במסקנא קאמר דבהכי פליגי:
notes.en: But the property is on lien to them: [the questioner] now holds that brothers who divided are heirs, and an oral loan is collected from heirs; or alternatively he holds that a loan written in the Torah is like one written in a document. But in the conclusion [the Gemara] says that this is exactly what they disagree about.

messages.text: Rather, it is referring to a case where the father died within thirty days of the birth of his sons, and the obligation of redemption applies to the firstborn himself, whose identity is unknown, but not to the father’s property.

If so, what is different about a case where they already divided the property between them, that Rabbi Meir deems them exempt? The reason must be that the priest will go to this son, and the son will reject him by demanding that the priest prove he is the firstborn; and likewise he will go to that other son, and he too will reject him in the same manner.

notes.he: ואומר אין אני בכור אלא אחי:
notes.en: And he puts him off: and says, “I am not the firstborn; my brother is.”

messages.text: The same should apply even in a case where they did not divide the property: Let the priest go to this son and he will reject him, and let him go to that son and he too will reject him.

notes.he: והא ליכא למימר דטריף נכסי משום אביהם דהא האב לא נתחייב כלום אלא בשביל הבנים טורפן ואמאי קתני אם נתנו כו' דמשמע דאם לא חלקו חייבין:
notes.en: Even when they did not divide, and so on: one cannot say that [the priest] seizes the property on account of their father, since the father was obligated in nothing; it is only on account of the sons that he would seize it. So why does the mishna teach “If they gave [before they divided]…”, which implies that if they have not divided, they are obligated?

messages.text: That is to say, i.e., it can be inferred from here, that in a case involving two people named Yosef ben Shimon who were residents of one city, and they acquired a field in partnership, a creditor of one of them can collect payment of his debt from either of them, despite the fact that he does not know which of them owes him the money.

The reason is that he can say to each of them: If I have a claim against you, I am taking the one hundred dinars that is your share in the joint field, and if I have a claim against the other Yosef ben Shimon, I am taking the one hundred dinars that is his share in the field. This is similar to the case in the mishna, as the brothers who have yet to divide their father’s property are considered partners, and therefore the priest can claim his debt from that property.

notes.he: שהיה איש אחד מוציא על אחד מהן שטר חוב וכל אחד מהן היה מדחהו לאמר לא אני הוא כי אם חבירי ולקחו בין שניהם שדה אחת טורף בעל חוב חציה דא"ל כו'. והכא נמי טורף הכהן ה' סלעים מהנכסים שהן יחד ואמר להו נמי הכי אם אתה הבכור מחלקך אני נוטל ואם אחיך הבכור מחלקו אני נוטל ובין שניכם תתפשרו:
notes.en: Two Yosef ben Shimons: a man produced a promissory note against one of them, and each put him off, saying, “It is not me but my fellow.” The two of them bought one field together: the creditor seizes half of it, since he says to him, and so on. Here too the priest seizes five sela from the property, which they hold together, and he likewise says to them: “If you are the firstborn, I take from your share, and if your brother is the firstborn, I take from his share; and between the two of you, settle it.”

notes.he: בעל חוב שיש לו שטר על יוסף בן שמעון גובה אותה מהן דאמר ליה אי בדידך כו':
notes.en: A creditor who holds a document against [a] Yosef ben Shimon collects it from them, since he says to him: “If it is yours…” and so on.

messages.text: Now consider the principle that a person’s property is a guarantee for him, i.e., it serves as a guarantee for the loan if the debtor does not repay it. Is there any case where one cannot claim repayment from the debtor himself, and yet he can claim from a guarantor?
messages.quote: a creditor of one of them can collect payment of his debt from either of them

notes.he: דכל חד וחד מדחי ליה:
notes.en: Whom he cannot claim from directly: since each one of them puts him off.

notes.dh: והני נכסים נמי כי לא חלקו הוי בשותפות
notes.he: אינון ערבין ביה שבעל חוב גובה מהן. מי איכא מידי דלדידיה לא מצי תבע דהא מת בתוך שלשים דאכתי לא איחייב בפדיון ולנכסיה דהוו ערב (לא) מצו תבעו והתנן המלוה כו'. וקי"ל דלא יתבע ערב תחילה אלא בעל חוב והכא בעל חוב לא מצי תבע:
notes.en: And this property too, while they have not divided it, is held in partnership. [Rava:] It is a guarantor for him, so that the creditor collects from it. Is there anything where one cannot claim from the man himself — for [the father] died within thirty days, when he was not yet obligated in the redemption — and yet one can claim from his property, which is a guarantor? [The printed text puts the word “not” here in parentheses, marking it as a word to delete.] But we learned: “One who lends…”, and we hold that one does not claim from the guarantor first, only from the debtor; and here one cannot claim from the debtor.

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Bava Batra 173a): In the case of one who lends money to another with the assurance of a guarantor, he cannot claim payment of the debt from the guarantor? And we maintain in this regard that he cannot claim payment of the debt from the guarantor at the outset, before first claiming the debt from the debtor. How, then, may the priest not claim the redemption money from either brother, and yet he can take it from their property?

notes.dh: לא יפרע וקיימא לן מאי לא יפרע דלא יתבע לערב תחלה
notes.he: עד שיתבע מן הלוה ולא יהא לו מה לפרוע:
notes.en: He shall not claim payment; and we hold: what does “he shall not claim payment” mean? That he may not claim from the guarantor first, until he has claimed from the borrower and the borrower has nothing to pay with.

messages.text: Actually, the mishna is referring to a case where the father died after thirty days following the birth of his sons and the property is already on lien for the mitzva of redemption. And if this is a case where there is a lot of property, so too, the halakha is that the priest takes the five sela coins from that property, even after the sons have divided it, as they are obligated to pay their father’s debt from their inheritance.

notes.he: אפי' חלקו דהא אישתעבדו נכסים בחיי האב ואע"פ שמלוה על פה היא גובה מן היורשין אם יש ירושה כשיעור החוב:
notes.en: So too he takes: even if they divided, since the property became on lien during the father’s lifetime; and although it is an oral loan, it is collected from the heirs if the inheritance is as large as the debt.

notes.he: ודאיכא נכסי טובא לכל חד וחד הכי נמי דשקיל אע"ג דחלקו:
notes.en: And where there is a lot of property for each one: so too he takes it, even though they divided.

messages.text: And what are we dealing with here? With a case where there is only the five sela coins received from their father. That was the entire estate.
And everyone accepts the opinion of Rav Asi,

notes.dh: דכולי עלמא אית להו דרב אסי כו'
notes.he: משמע הכא דר"מ מספקא ליה אי אית ברירה או לא כרב אסי ותימה דר"מ לית ליה ברירה בההיא דהלוקח יין מן הכותים ובמרובה (ב"ק סט:) ובפרק כל הגט (גיטין כה.) ורבא גופיה דמוקי להו הכא כרב אסי יש לתמוה דבפ' כל הגט (גיטין כו.) ק דבין ר' יהודה בין ר"ש אית להו ברירה ויש לחלק דיש ברירה היכא דמתני בפירוש כגון שני לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש והריני בועליך על מנת שירצה אבא וזה גטיך אם מתי ובהכי מתרצא קושיא דשמואל אדשמואל דלית ליה ברירה בסוף ביצה (דף לז:) גבי שנים שלקחו בהמה בשותפות ובההיא דמי שאחזו (גיטין דף עה:) דאיתקין שמואל בגיטא דשכיב מרע אית ליה ברירה והוי גיטא לכי מיית כדדייק בריש כל הגט:
notes.en: And everyone accepts the opinion of Rav Asi, and so on: this implies that Rabbi Meir is unsure whether there is retroactive clarification [bereira] or not, like Rav Asi. This is puzzling, since Rabbi Meir does not accept bereira in the case of one who buys wine from Samaritans, [cited] in chapter Merubba (Bava Kamma 69b) and in chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 25a). And it is puzzling about Rava himself, who here sets them both as following Rav Asi, since in chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 26a) [it is stated] that both Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon accept bereira. One may distinguish: there is bereira where one stipulates explicitly, for example “the two log that I will separate in the future”, “I am having relations with you on condition that father consents”, and “this is your bill of divorce if I die”. This also resolves the contradiction between one statement of Shmuel and another: he does not accept bereira at the end of Beitza (37b), regarding two who bought an animal in partnership; yet in chapter Mi SheAḥazo (Gittin 75b), where Shmuel instituted [a condition] for the bill of divorce of a dangerously ill man, he accepts bereira, and it is a bill of divorce [effective] from when he dies, as is deduced at the beginning of Kol HaGet.

messages.text: In the case of brothers who divided property they received as an inheritance, with regard to half of it they are considered heirs and with regard to the other half they are considered purchasers from each other.

notes.he: כדאיתא בב"ק בפ' ראשון (דף ט.):
notes.en: Of Rav Asi: as found in Bava Kamma, chapter one (9a).

notes.he: דמספקא ליה אם ברירה ויורשין נינהו או אין ברירה ולקוחות נינהו הלכך מחצה יורשין ומחצה לקוחות:
notes.en: Half heirs and half purchasers: since he is unsure whether there is retroactive clarification [bereira], in which case they are heirs, or there is no retroactive clarification, in which case they are purchasers; therefore they are half heirs and half purchasers.

notes.dh: דאמר רב אסי אחין שחלקו מחצה יורשין כו'
notes.he: מילתא דרב אסי איתא בפרק קמא דב"ק (דף ט.) ובבבא בתרא בסוף בית כור (בבא בתרא דף קז.) דפליגי התם באחין שחלקו ובא בעל חוב וטרף חלקו של אחד מהם דרב אמר בטלה מחלוקת דיורשין הם ושמואל אמר ויתר דלקוחות הן ושלא באחריות ורב אסי מספקא בנכסים הנשארים (אלא שאינו) חלקו דהוא רביע הנכסים נוטל בקרקע וחצי האחר במעות משום דמספקא ליה אי כיורשין ונוטל הכל בקרקע או כלקוחות באחריות ויכול לסלקו במעות ולפירוש זה לא יתכן גירסת רבינו חננאל דגרס בפ' בית כור (שם) שלשה אחין ויש מפרש שנוטל חצי חלקו הראוי לו ורביע חלקו נוטל בקרקע ורביע במעות וחצי חלקו מפסיד משום דאם הוא יורש יש לו ליטול חלק משלם ואם שלא באחריות יש לו להפסיד ונוטל חצי חלקו מספק ומה שנוטל נמי מספקא לן אם מכח ירושה נוטל ויש לו ליקח הכל בקרקע או מכח דהוי כלוקח באחריות ונוטל במעות הלכך נוטל מחצה בקרקע דהיינו רביע ומחצה במעות וקשה לפירוש זה דהשתא אי לא הוה לספוקי לן אלא אי כיורשין אי כלקוחות שלא באחריות נוטל חלקו בקרקע ומשום דאיכא נמי לספוקי דאפילו אי הוה לוקח שמא לוקח באחריות הוא הורע כחו אדרבה הוה לן לומר דחצי חלקו יטול בקרקע והרביע במעות ועוד דמוקמינן הכא מתני' כגון דליכא אלא חמשה סלעים ואי לא חשיב להו רב אסי כיורשין אלא ברביע אפילו יש שם עשר סלעים פטורים שלא יכול לגבות הכהן כי אם הרביע דהוו בהו כיורשים והיינו חצי חמש וללשון ראשון שפירש בקונטרס בב"ק (דף ט.) שנוטל חצי חלקו בקרקע או במעות משום דמספקא לן אי הוו כיורשין או לקוחות שלא באחריות אותו לשון נמי יתכן בין גירסת שני אחין בין גירסת שלשה ומיהו קשיא מנא ליה להש"ס שמספקא לרב אסי כלל ביורשין דלמא פשיטא דלאו יורשין נינהו אלא מספקא ליה אי הוו כלקוחות באחריות או כלקוחות שלא באחריות ועוד דלא הוה שייך למיתני תרי זימני רביע כיון דאו או קתני וכלשון אחרון נראה ולא יתכן לגרוס כלל שלשה אחין דמאי אית ליה למינקט שלשה אי הוה נקט חמשה אורחיה דהש"ס הוא בכל דוכתי כמו היו חמשה תובעין אותו ה' נשים שנתערבו ולדותיהן כל אחד מחמשה אבל שלשה לאו אורחיה למינקט כיון שכך שוין שנים כשלשה וא"ת מאחר דמספקא ליה לרב אסי אי כיורשין הוו אי כלקוחות לימא המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה דאפילו לסומכוס לא מסתבר הכא לומר חולקין בספק זה בזה שחכמים מסופקים בהוראה וי"ל שיש דברים דהיכא דהדין מסופק לחכמים כי הכא עשו אותו כודאי פלגא הכי ופלגא הכי כדאשכחן נמי בפרק השוכר את האומנים (ב"מ פג.) גבי הני דדרו באגרא לישלם פלגא קרוב לפשיעה וקרוב לאונס דמה נפשך או כוליה פשיעה או כוליה אונס ואי מספקא לן ה"ל למימר המע"ה וכן בפ' מי שמת (ב"ב קמה.) דקאמר ר' יוסי קדשה בעשרים נותן לו שלשים חצאין דמספקא ליה אי קדושין לטיבועין או לא ועושה כאילו ודאי מחצה לטיבועין ומחצה לאו לטיבועין ובפ' יש נוחלין (בבא בתרא קכו.) גבכור דאמרינן ובמלוה שעמו פליגי ולפירוש זה אתיא נמי שפיר ההוא דמרחץ דהשואל בסוף הפ' (ב"מ קב.) דקאמר יחלקו את חדש העיבור לכולי עלמא ולא צריך לאוקמה כסומכוס ויש דברים שאמרו חכמים והשתא דלא איתמר הלכתא לא כמר ולא כמר דעבד כמר עבד ודעבד כמר עבד ויש דברים שאמרו חכמים שודא דדייני כי התם בריש המוכר את הבית (ב"ב סב: ושם) דאמרי לה להאי גיסא ואמרי לה להאי גיסא שודא דדייני:
notes.en: In brief: Rav Asi’s statement is found in Bava Kamma chapter one (9a) and in Bava Batra (107a). There Rav and Shmuel disagree about brothers who divided, after which a creditor seized one brother’s share: Rav says the division is void, since they are heirs; Shmuel says that brother has lost out, since they are purchasers without a guarantee; and Rav Asi is unsure. Tosafot weighs two explanations of Rav Asi. First: of the remaining property he takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money, since it is unclear whether he is like an heir (who takes it all in land) or like a purchaser with a guarantee (who can be paid off in money); on this explanation Rabbeinu Ḥananel’s reading “three brothers” (Bava Batra 107a) cannot stand. Second: he takes half of his proper share, a quarter in land and a quarter in money, and loses the other half. Tosafot objects to the second: if the only doubt were heir versus purchaser without a guarantee, he would take his [half] share in land; should the added doubt that he might be a purchaser with a guarantee weaken him? On the contrary, he should take half his share in land and the quarter in money. Further, our daf sets the mishna where there are only five sela; if Rav Asi counted them heirs for only a quarter, they would be exempt even with ten sela, since the priest could collect only the quarter in which they are heirs, which is half of five. Rashi’s first explanation in Bava Kamma (9a), that he takes half his share, in land or in money, fits either reading. Yet one may ask how the Talmud knows that Rav Asi doubts whether they are heirs at all; perhaps he only doubts whether they are purchasers with or without a guarantee. And “a quarter” would not be stated twice, since it is taught as “either… or”. The last explanation seems right, and the reading “three brothers” should be rejected altogether: the Talmud’s way is to speak of five (five claimants, five women whose offspring were intermingled), not three, since two are the same as three. If you ask: since Rav Asi is unsure whether they are heirs or purchasers, why not rule that the burden of proof rests on the one who would take from his fellow? Even Sumakhos would not divide here, for this is a doubt of the Sages about the ruling. Answer: there are matters where, when the law is in doubt for the Sages, they treat it as certainly half one way and half the other, as in Bava Metzia 83a (porters who must pay half, as close to negligence and close to accident), Bava Batra 145a (Rabbi Yosei: he betrothed with twenty and is repaid thirty halves), Bava Batra 126a (the firstborn and a loan owed to the estate), and Bava Metzia 102a (the bathhouse, where they divide the intercalated month according to everyone, without needing Sumakhos). There are also matters where, since no halakha was stated, whoever acts like either master has acted properly; and matters left to the judges’ discretion, as in Bava Batra 62b. notes.he: שהקנה זה לזה חלקו בשביל מה שתופש:
notes.en: Half heirs and half purchasers: for each one conveyed his share to the other in return for what he takes.

messages.text: And furthermore, everyone agrees that a loan written in the Torah, i.e., a financial obligation by Torah law, such as the redemption of the firstborn,

notes.he: כגון פדיון הבן ה' סלעים דזכי ליה רחמנא לכהן:
notes.en: A loan written in the Torah: such as the five sela of the redemption of a son, which the Merciful One awarded to the priest.

notes.dh: ודכולי עלמא מלוה הכתובה בתורה לאו ככתובה בשטר דמיא
notes.he: גם במסקנא יהיה כן דאמרינן בדרב אסי או בדרב פפא קמיפלגי דמשמע אי כולהו אית להו דרב אסי ודרב פפא היו פטורין מטעם חמש ולא חצי חמש ותימה דלקמן בפירקין (בכורות דף מט:) אמר דרבי יהודה סבר ככתובה בשטר דמיא ועוד קשה למאי דמסקינן בדרב פפא קמיפלגי דלית ליה לרבי יהודה דרב פפא אלמא קסבר דמלוה על פה גובה אף מן הלקוחות אטו מי לית ליה לר' יהודה הא דתנן בגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעה.) המלוה את חבירו בשטר גובה מנכסים משועבדים על פה גובה מן בני חורין ועיקר מילתיה דרב פפא לאו איתמר אלא לאשמועינן דגובה מן היורשים לאפוקי מדרב ושמואל דאמרי מלוה על פה אינו גובה לא מן היורשין ולא מן הלקוחות אבל למאי דאינו גובה מן הלקוחות זה אינו שום חידוש ודבר פשוט הוא בכל הש"ס ונראה לפרש לפי המסקנא דלאו ממש כרב פפא קאמר אלא כמלוה על פה כי הך דפדיון הבן כשהיא כתובה ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף כט:) איתא להא דלקמן וגרסינן שם ר' יהודה לטעמיה דאמר מלוה הכתובה בתורה ככתובה בשטר דמיא והיינו לטעמא דהכא אי נמי בדרב פפא ממש קמיפלגי דרב פפא גופיה צריך לומר דאיירי נמי במלוה הכתובה בתורה דבפרק קמא דקדושין (דף יג:) קאמר רב פפא הלכתא מלוה על פה גובה מן היורשין שיעבודא דאורייתא ובפ' גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעו.) מפרש טעמא שלא תנעול דלת בפני לווין וצ"ל דבקדושין איירי במלוה הכתובה בתורה דקסבר גובה מן היורשים ולא מן הלקוחות ובההיא איירינן הכא דר' יהודה לית ליה דרב פפא וקסבר דגובה מן הלקוחות:
notes.en: In brief: And everyone agrees that a loan written in the Torah is not like one written in a document: this holds in the conclusion too, which says they disagree about Rav Asi or about Rav Pappa; that implies that if both accepted Rav Asi and Rav Pappa, they would be exempt because of “five, not half of five”. This is puzzling, since below in this chapter (49b) it says that Rabbi Yehuda holds a loan written in the Torah is like one written in a document. A further difficulty: on the conclusion that they disagree about Rav Pappa, Rabbi Yehuda rejects Rav Pappa and holds that an oral loan is collected even from purchasers. Does Rabbi Yehuda reject the mishna in Get Pashut (Bava Batra 175a), “One who lends with a document collects from mortgaged property; orally, from unencumbered property”? Moreover, Rav Pappa’s main point was not that, but that an oral loan is collected from heirs, against Rav and Shmuel, who say it is collected neither from heirs nor from purchasers; that it is not collected from purchasers is no novelty, being plain throughout the Talmud. Tosafot explains: according to the conclusion, it is not exactly Rav Pappa that is meant, but [a debt] like an oral loan, such as this redemption of a son, though it is written [in the Torah]. In Kiddushin chapter one (29b) the passage below is found, and there the reading is “Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning, for he says a loan written in the Torah is like one written in a document”, which fits the reasoning here. Alternatively, they do disagree about Rav Pappa himself, and Rav Pappa must be speaking of a loan written in the Torah: in Kiddushin chapter one (13b) Rav Pappa says the halakha is that an oral loan is collected from heirs, since the lien is by Torah law, while in Get Pashut (Bava Batra 176a) the reason given is “so as not to lock the door before borrowers”. So Kiddushin must be speaking of a loan written in the Torah, holding that it is collected from heirs but not from purchasers; and that is the ruling Rabbi Yehuda rejects here, holding that it is collected even from purchasers. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: היינו דוקא כגון פדיון הבן וערכין ונזקין וכיוצא בהן שלא נתחייבו אם לא שחייבתו תורה אבל מלוה על פה אע"ג דכתיב (דברים כ״ד:י״א) האיש אשר אתה נושה בו יוציא אליך את העבוט לא (מקרא) כתובה להיות כתובה בשטר ואע"ג דאיירי על פה דלא חייבתו ממה שכתובה בתורה כיון דבלאו הכי פשיטא הוא שיש לו לשלם מה שהלווהו:
notes.en: A loan written in the Torah: this means specifically such things as the redemption of a son, valuations, damages and the like, which one would not owe had the Torah not obligated him. But an ordinary oral loan, even though it is written “the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge out to you” (Deuteronomy 24:11), and even though that verse speaks of an oral loan, does not count as “written” so as to be like one written in a document, since the Torah did not create the obligation by writing it; even without the verse it is obvious that he must repay what he was lent.

notes.he: כגון ה' סלעים של בכור:
notes.en: A loan written in the Torah: such as the five sela of a firstborn.

messages.text: is not like one written in a document, but like an oral loan. And everyone accepts the opinion of Rav Pappa,
When a creditor gives a loan by oral agreement, he can collect the debt from the heirs of the debtor after his death but he cannot collect the debt from the purchasers of the debtor’s property.

Consequently, the priest can collect the redemption money only from the half of the property with regard to which the sons are considered heirs, and since the entire property is worth only five sela coins he would be able to take only two and a half sela coins.
And here Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree with regard to the issue of: Five, but not with half of five.
As Rabbi Meir holds that the Torah requires giving specifically five sela coins, but not half or part of five; therefore, the brothers are exempt from giving a priest those two and a half sela coins.

notes.he: הלכך פטורין דכיון דחלקו הוה ליה מחצה לקוחות ולא אישתאר ירושה אלא ב' סלעים ופלגא ומפלגא דלקוחות לא שקיל איהו מידי דמלוה על פה לא גביא מלקוחות:
notes.en: And not half of five: therefore they are exempt. Since they divided, they are half purchasers, and only two and a half sela remain as inheritance; and from the purchasers’ half he takes nothing, since an oral loan is not collected from purchasers.

notes.he: ולא דמי לחמשה בקר דמסקינן (ב"ק דף עא:) אפילו חמשה חצאי בקר אמר רחמנא דתשלומין נינהו ויש לו לשלם מה שהוא חייב אבל הכא מצות חמש סלעים רחמנא רמי עליה ולא מקיימא בפחות מחמש אע"פ שיכול לשלם לעשרה כהנים בזה אחר זה לא דמי הכא דלא משתעבד אלא בחצי חמש:
notes.en: For Rabbi Meir holds five: this is not like “five cattle” [Exodus 21:37], where we conclude (Bava Kamma 71b) that the Merciful One meant even five halves of cattle, because those are payments, and he must pay what he owes. Here, though, the Merciful One placed on him a mitzva of five sela, and it is not fulfilled with less than five. And although one may pay [the five sela] to ten priests one after another, that is not comparable here, since here he is liable for only half of five.

notes.he: ר' מאיר סבר ה' סלעים הוא דבעי למיהב לכהן ולא חצי ה' להכי קאמר ר' מאיר חלקו פטורין דקא הוו מחצה לקוחות ולא משעבדי ליה:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir holds that it is five sela that one must give the priest, and not half of five; that is why Rabbi Meir says that if they divided they are exempt, since they are half purchasers and [that half] is not on lien to him.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yehuda maintains that the Torah requires giving five sela coins, and even half or part of five. Therefore, he rules that the priest takes those two and a half sela coins from the property with regard to which the sons are considered heirs.

notes.he: ושקיל ההוא פלגא דהוי ירושה:
notes.en: And even half of five: and he takes the half that is inheritance.

notes.he: דאמר נתחייבו נכסים אפי' כי חלקו סבר חמש ואפי' חצי חמש:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda, who says the obligation took effect on the property even when they divided, holds five and even half of five.

messages.text: If so, when Rabbi Yehuda says: The obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property of the father, he should have said that the obligation to redeem the firstborn took effect on the man, i.e., the brothers who are obligated to pay the sum, as Rabbi Yehuda agrees that the priest forfeits the half of the obligation that applies to the property.
messages.quote: The obligation took effect on the property

notes.he: דלר' יהודה פלגא הוא דשקיל נתחייבו הנכסים בתמיה:
notes.en: If so: that according to Rabbi Yehuda he takes only half, [can he say] “the obligation took effect on the property”? [A rhetorical question.]

notes.dh: חייב גברא מיבעי ליה גרסינן ולא גרסינן נתחייב
notes.he: כלומר הכי איבעי ליה למיתנא רבי יהודה אומר חייבין שאינן פטורין לגמרי כדאמרי' אלא חצי חמש מיהא מיחייבי ולא שייך למיתני נתחייבו הנכסים (דאית ליה) מאחר שלאחר שלשים מת אלא בשביל החלוקה שחלקו ונעשו לקוחות הפסיד הכהן לר' יהודה גופיה ממה שנתחייבו הנכסים הפסיד מחצה:
notes.en: We read “he should have said, the man is obligated”, and we do not read “became obligated”. That is: Rabbi Yehuda should have taught “they are obligated”, meaning they are not entirely exempt, as we said, but are at least obligated for half of five. It does not fit to teach “the property became obligated”, since [on this reading] he died after thirty days; rather, because of the division they made, by which they became purchasers, the priest has lost, according to Rabbi Yehuda himself, half of what the property had been obligated for.

notes.he: דלאחר ל' קא מיירי נתחייב גברא מיבעי ליה:
notes.en: If so: that it speaks of [a father who died] after thirty [days], he should have said “the man is obligated”.

messages.text: In a case where the identity of the firstborn is unknown, and the brothers divided their father’s property, if there are ten dinars, which equals two and a half sela coins, for this brother, and ten dinars for that brother, they are obligated to pay the priest; and if not, they are exempt.
messages.lead: And furthermore, it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: ושניהם ספק בכורות:
notes.en: Brothers who divided: and each of the two may be the firstborn.

notes.dh: עשרה זוז לזה ועשרה זוז לזה
notes.he: דהיינו ב' סלעים ופלגא:
notes.en: Ten dinars for this one and ten dinars for that one: which is two and a half sela.

notes.dh: עשרה זוז לזה ועשרה זוז לזה
notes.he: דהיינו כ' זוז שהן ה' סלעים:
notes.en: Ten dinars for this one and ten dinars for that one: that is, twenty dinars, which are five sela.

messages.text: What is the meaning of the clause: Ten dinars for this brother and ten dinars for that brother?
messages.quote: ten dinars for this brother, and ten dinars for that brother

messages.text: If we say each has ten dinars from the father’s property, which is the total sum of both the half of the inheritance and the half with regard to which they are purchasers together, which equals two and a half sela coins, and Rabbi Yehuda says they are obligated to pay the priest because he maintains that there is a mitzva to give five sela coins and even half or part of five, this is difficult.

notes.dh: אילימא בין חלק הירושה בין חלק הלקוחות
notes.he: והא דקתני חייבין פלגא דחמשה קאמר דהא אמרת דכולי עלמא אית להו דרב אסי ורב פפא ושמעינן מינה דחמש ואפילו חצי חמש:
notes.en: If we say, both the inheritance share and the purchase share: and when it teaches “they are obligated”, it means for half of five, since you said that everyone accepts Rav Asi and Rav Pappa; and we learn from it [that Rabbi Yehuda holds] five, and even half of five.

notes.he: ה' ואפי' חצי ה' וכיון דפחות מה' מצי יהיב חצי לאו דוקא הוא אלא ואפי' פחות מחצי:
notes.en: If so, five and even half of five: and since he may give less than five, “half” is not meant exactly; rather, even less than half.

messages.text: If so, why specifically state that they are obligated only when there are ten dinars? The same halakha would apply even to fewer than ten dinars, as the priest is entitled to whatever is available.

notes.he: אלא שמונה דלא מטי לכהן אלא ב' סלעים שקיל להו דהואיל ושקיל כהן בציר מחמש כל מה דמיתרמי ליה שקיל דהא דאמרי' חצי חמש ה"ה לרבות חמש ושליש חמש ואמאי קתני אם לאו פטורין:
notes.en: Even fewer than ten: say eight, where only two sela reach the priest; he should take them, for once the priest takes less than five, he takes whatever comes his way; “half of five” equally includes a third of five. So why does it teach “and if not, they are exempt”?

notes.he: דאפי' חצי ה' מאי איריא עשרה זוז:
notes.en: If so: that [he holds] even half of five, why specifically ten dinars?

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that in this case there are ten dinars of inheritance for this brother and ten dinars of inheritance for that brother, which totals five sela coins. According to Rabbi Yehuda, it is only in this case that they are obligated to pay the priest. Evidently, Rabbi Yehuda maintains that there is a mitzva to give specifically five sela coins, but not half or part of five, which contradicts the suggested explanation of the dispute.

notes.he: לכל חד וחד לבר מפלגא דלקוחות דהוי חמש סלעים דירושה:
notes.en: Rather, it is obvious: ten dinars of inheritance for each one, apart from the purchasers’ half, which makes five sela of inheritance.

notes.he: אלא פשיטא עשרה זוז דירושה לכל אחד וה' סלעים ניגבין מהן מירושתן אלמא דה' ולא חצי ה' סבירא ליה לר' יהודה:
notes.en: Rather, it is obvious: ten dinars of inheritance for each, and the five sela are collected from them out of their inheritance; evidently Rabbi Yehuda holds five and not half of five.

messages.text: Rather, the mishna is referring to a case where the father’s property is worth five sela coins, and everyone, both Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, agree that the Torah requires giving five sela coins, but not half of five.

And here they disagree with regard to the statements of Rav Asi and Rav Pappa that the portion of the inheritance includes only two and a half sela, which the priest is not entitled to collect. Rabbi Meir holds in accordance with their opinion, while Rabbi Yehuda disagrees and holds that all five sela coins are available for the redemption.

notes.he: במתניתין בדרב אסי או בדרב פפא פליגי דר"מ אית ליה דרב אסי ורב פפא הואיל דבין הכל אין שם אלא חמש לא שקיל מידי דחמש ולא חצי חמש ור' יהודה אית ליה דרב אסי דפלגא הוי לקוחות ולית ליה דרב פפא אלא סבירא ליה דמלוה על פה גובה מן הלקוחות ושקיל כולהו א"נ לית ליה דרב אסי אלא כולהו הוי ירושה ושקיל כולה. והשתא דהכי ס"ל מוקמינן לה לברייתא אם יש שם י' זוז לזה וי' זוז לזה בין הכל חייבין לתת כל הנכסים ואם לאו דבין הכל ליכא חמש פטורין דחמש ולא חצי חמש:
notes.en: And here: in the mishna, they disagree about Rav Asi or about Rav Pappa. Rabbi Meir accepts both Rav Asi and Rav Pappa; since there are only five [sela] in all, [the priest] takes nothing, [for it is] five and not half of five. Rabbi Yehuda accepts Rav Asi, that half is purchase, but rejects Rav Pappa, holding that an oral loan is collected from purchasers, and so the priest takes all of it. Alternatively, he rejects Rav Asi, and all of it is inheritance, and the priest takes all of it. And now that this is his view, we read the baraita this way: if there are ten dinars for this one and ten dinars for that one, all together, they must give all the property; and if not, if there are not five [sela] in all, they are exempt, [for it is] five and not half of five.

notes.he: בדר' אסי ורב פפא קמיפלגי כלומר אי תרויהו סבירא להו דרב פפא פליגי בדרב אסי דאי סברי כרב אסי דאמר האחין שחלקו מחצה יורשין ומחצה לקוחות פליגי בדרב פפא דר' מאיר סבר כרב פפא דמלוה על פה אינו גובה מן הלקוחות להכי קאמר חלקו פטורין היכא דליכא אלא ה' סלעים דחמש אמר רחמנא ולא חצי ה'. ור' יהודה לית ליה דרב פפא דאפי' מן הלקוחות נגבין דנתחייבו נכסים. ואי תרוויהו סברי לה כרב פפא דאמר מלוה ע"פ אינה גובה מן הלקוחות פליגי בדרב אסי דר"י לא סבר כרב אסי אלא כולהו יורשין נינהו וכולהו ה' סלעים מצי למיגבי דנתחייבו נכסים:
notes.en: They disagree about Rav Asi and Rav Pappa. That is: if both of them accept Rav Pappa, they disagree about Rav Asi; and if they accept Rav Asi, who says brothers who divided are half heirs and half purchasers, they disagree about Rav Pappa. Rabbi Meir holds like Rav Pappa, that an oral loan is not collected from purchasers; that is why he says that if they divided they are exempt where there are only five sela, since the Merciful One said five, and not half of five. And Rabbi Yehuda rejects Rav Pappa, [holding that the money] is collected even from purchasers, since the property became obligated. And if both hold like Rav Pappa, that an oral loan is not collected from purchasers, they disagree about Rav Asi: Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rav Asi; rather, they are all heirs, and he can collect all five sela, since the property became obligated.

messages.text: If one had two sons and it is unknown which is the firstborn, and the father died, Rabbi Yehuda says the obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property of the father. Therefore, even if the father’s property has been divided, the sons are required to pay the priest.
messages.lead: And there are those who teach this discussion with regard to the latter clause of the mishna:
messages.quote: The obligation took effect on the property

notes.dh: איכא דמתני לה לכולה הך שמעתא אסיפא
notes.he: דמתניתין דמילתיה דרבי יהודה:
notes.en: There are those who teach this entire discussion on the latter clause: of the mishna, the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: When did the father die? If we say that he died after thirty days following the birth of his sons, should one conclude by inference that Rabbi Meir maintains that if they divided their father’s property they are exempt from giving the redemption payment to the priest? But the property is already on lien for the mitzva of redemption.

Rather, it is referring to a case where the father died within thirty days of the birth of his sons and the obligation of redemption applies to the firstborn himself, though it is unknown which is the firstborn.

If so, why does Rabbi Yehuda obligate them even when the brothers had already divided their father’s property between them? Let the priest go to this son, and he will reject him, by claiming that he is not the firstborn, and let him go to that son and he too will reject him on the same grounds.

That is to say: In a case involving two people named Yosef ben Shimon, who were residents of one city, and one of them purchased a field from the other, an earlier creditor can collect payment of his debt from that field.

notes.he: הכא נמי דסבירא לן האחין שחלקו לקוחות הן דאין ברירה דקמחייב להו ר' יהודה:
notes.en: And one of them bought a field from the other: here too, since we hold that brothers who divided are purchasers, as there is no bereira, [this is the case] where Rabbi Yehuda obligates them.

messages.text: This is because he can say to the buyer: If you are indebted to me I am taking the one hundred dinars that is your share in the field, and if the other Yosef ben Shimon is indebted to me, then this field was on lien to me before you acquired it.

notes.he: ולקח אחד מהן שדה מחברו האי דמי לחלקו דאידך לית חילק בה ובעל חוב גובה ממנו דאמר ליה אי בדידך כו'. הם הכי נמי אמר כהן לכל חד מהני אחין אי את בכור מנתא דידך שקילנא. ואי אחוך בכור משעבדי לי נכסי מיקמי דידך:
notes.en: And one of them bought a field from the other: this is like their having divided, since the other has no share in it, and the creditor collects from [the buyer], since he says to him, “If it is yours…” and so on. So too the priest says to each of these brothers: “If you are the firstborn, I take your portion; and if your brother is the firstborn, the property was on lien to me before you [acquired it].”

messages.text: Now consider, a person’s property is a guarantee for him, so why can the creditor not claim his debt from the debtor himself but can claim it from the guarantor, i.e., his property?
messages.quote: an earlier creditor can collect payment of his debt from that field

messages.text: And from here onward, all the rest of the discussion is the same as in the first version of the passage, as cited earlier.

notes.he: אלא בדרב אסי ורב פפא פליגי:
notes.en: As in the first version: [ending with] “Rather, they disagree about Rav Asi and Rav Pappa.”

notes.he: וכולהי קשייתא דאקשינן ברישא עד אי הכי בתרא וכדתריצנא אלא בדרב אסי ורב פפא קא מיפלגי:
notes.en: Rava said: Now consider, and so on: and all the difficulties we raised in the first version, up to the last “If so”, and as we resolved it: rather, they disagree about Rav Asi and Rav Pappa.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to two wives of one man, both of whom had not previously given birth, and they gave birth to two males, i.e., each bore one male, and the sons were intermingled, the father gives ten sela coins to the priest even if it is unknown which son was born first, because it is certain that each is firstborn of his mother.

notes.he: של אחד:
notes.en: Mishna. Two wives: of one man.

notes.he: במחבא שנתערבו:
notes.en: And they gave birth to two males: out of sight, so that they were intermingled.

messages.text: In a case where one of them dies within thirty days of birth, if he gave all ten sela coins to one priest, the priest must return five sela to him, because the father was not obligated to redeem the son who then died.

notes.he: האב פדיון שניהם יחזיר לו ה' סלעים הואיל ומת בתוך ל' ואיגלאי מילתא דנפל הוא ושלא כדין שקל:
notes.en: If he gave to one priest: the father [gave] the redemption of both, [the priest] must return five sela to him, since [one child] died within thirty days and it became clear that it was a nonviable birth, and [the priest] took it without right.

messages.text: And if he gave the redemption payment to two different priests, he cannot reclaim the money from the possession of either priest, as each could claim that the money that he received was for the living child.

notes.he: דכל חד וחד מדחי ליה ואומר הריני מחזיק בם בשביל פדיון החי:
notes.en: He cannot take it back from them: since each one puts him off and says, “I am holding them for the redemption of the living one.”

notes.dh: ואם לשני כהנים נתן אין יכול להוציא מידם
notes.he: וא"ת כיון דאם לא נתן אין זקוק ליתן השתא נמי דנתן נמי ליהוי כתקפו כהן דמוציאין מידו כדאמר בפרק שנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף ו:) והכא ניחא טפי דאין יודע ממי להוציא אבל לקמן קשה טפי גבי מת ביום שלשים דקאמר ר' עקיבא אם נתן לא יטול ואם לא נתן לא יתן דכיון דאם לא נתן לא יתן השתא נמי כשנתן ליהוי כתקפו כהן וי"ל כיון דמתחלה נותן לו בתורת מתנות כהונה אע"פ שאח"כ נתגלה שאם לא נטל לא היה ראוי ליטלו מספק לא אמרינן מוציאין מידו וכן ההוא דבא באמצע החדש בסוף השואל (ב"מ דף קב:) דאע"ג דבתחלת החדש כולו למשכיר לא מדמינן ליה לתקפו כהן:
notes.en: And if he gave to two priests, he cannot take it back from them: and if you say: since had he not given he would not be required to give, now that he has given, let it be like a case where a priest seized [gifts by force], where we take it away from him, as is said in chapter Shenayim Oḥazin (Bava Metzia 6b)? Here it is easier, since he does not know from whom to take it back. But below it is harder, regarding a child who died on the thirtieth day, where Rabbi Akiva says: if he gave, he shall not take it back, and if he did not give, he need not give. Since if he did not give he need not give, now too that he gave, let it be like a priest who seized! One may answer: since at the outset he gives it to him as a priestly gift, then even though it later became clear that, had the priest not taken it, it would not have been right to take it out of doubt, we do not say we take it away from him. So too the case of one who arrives in the middle of the month, at the end of [chapter] HaShoel (Bava Metzia 102b): even though at the start of the month it all belongs to the landlord, we do not compare it to a priest who seized.

notes.he: אינו יכול להוציא מידן דכל חד מצי אמר אנא נקיטנא פדיון דחי:
notes.en: [On the mishna of 48b, two priests:] He cannot take it back from them: since each [priest] can say, “What I hold is the redemption of the living one.”

messages.text: If one mother gave birth to a male and one gave birth to a female, or if between them they gave birth to two males and one female, and the children were intermingled, the father gives five sela coins to the priest: In the first case because the male might have preceded the female and in the second case because one of the males is certainly firstborn.

notes.he: ילדו הנשים שלו במחבא נותן ה' סלעים לכהן דממה נפשך חד הוי בכור אם האחת ילדה שני זכרים הראשון בכור ואם האחת ילדה זכר ונקבה נמצא שחבירתה ילדה זכר לבדו והוא בכור ואותו שעם הנקבה פטור שמא נקבה יצאת ראשון והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: Or two males and a female: his wives gave birth out of sight. He gives five sela to the priest, since either way one is a firstborn: if one wife bore two males, the first is a firstborn; and if one bore a male and a female, then her fellow bore a male alone, and he is a firstborn; and the one born with the female is exempt, since perhaps the female came out first, and the burden of proof rests on the one who would take from his fellow.

notes.he: שאחת ילדה זכר (ונקב' שאחת ילדה זכר) ואחת נקבה או ב' זכרים ונקבה שאחת ילדה זכר ונקבה ואחת זכר נותן ה' סלעים לכהן בשביל ההיא דילדה זכר לחוד:
notes.en: [On the mishna of 48b:] A male and a female: where one [wife] bore a male and the other a female; or two males and a female, where one bore a male and a female and the other a male: he gives five sela to the priest on account of the one who bore a male alone. [A phrase repeated in the printed text is left out.]

messages.text: If the children were two females and a male, or two males and two females, the priest has nothing here, as it is possible the female was born first to each mother.

notes.he: דאיכא למימר הנקבות יצאו תחלה ואין כאן בכור:
notes.en: The priest has nothing here: since one can say the females came out first, and there is no firstborn here.

notes.he: שהאחת ילדה זכר ונקבה והאחת נקבה או כל אחת זכר ונקבה אין כאן לכהן כלום:
notes.en: [On the mishna of 48b:] Two females and a male: where one bore a male and a female and the other a female; or [two males and two females, where] each bore a male and a female: the priest has nothing here.

messages.text: If one of his wives had previously given birth and one had not previously given birth and they gave birth to two males who became intermingled, the father gives five sela coins to the priest, as it is certain that one of them was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.
If one of them dies within thirty days of birth the father is exempt from that payment, as it is possible that the one who died was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

notes.he: דמצי למימר בן המבכרת מת:
notes.en: The father is exempt: since he can say, “The son of the one giving birth for the first time is the one who died.”

notes.he: ונתערבו האב פטור דהמוציא מחברו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: [On the mishna of 48b, apparently the case of one wife who had given birth before and one who had not:] And they bore two males, and they were intermingled: the father is exempt, since the burden of proof rests on the one who would take from his fellow.

messages.text: In a case of intermingling where the father died and the sons are alive,

If they gave the five sela coins to the priest before they divided their father’s property between them, they gave it, and it remains in the possession of the priest. But if not, they are exempt from giving the redemption payment to the priest.

notes.he: כדין אותו של מעלה משום דרב אסי ורב פפא:
notes.en: If they gave before they divided, and so on: like the ruling of the case above, because of Rav Asi and Rav Pappa.

notes.dh: אם נתנו עד שלא חלקו כו'
notes.he: צריך שום צריכותא אמאי קתני בתרוייהו פלוגתא דר"מ ורבי יהודה:
notes.en: If they gave before they divided, and so on: some explanation is needed of why it is necessary to teach the dispute of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda in both [mishnayot].

messages.text: The obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property of the father.
If the wives gave birth to a male and a female the priest has nothing here, as perhaps the female was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

notes.he: יש לומר אותה שלא בכרה ילדה הנקבה ואין כאן בכור:
notes.en: A male and a female: one can say that the one who had not given birth bore the female, and there is no firstborn here.

messages.text: With regard to two women who had not previously given birth, who were married to two different men, and they gave birth to two males and the sons were intermingled, this father gives five sela coins to a priest and that father gives five sela coins to a priest, as each is certainly firstborn to his mother.

notes.he: של ב' אנשים שלא בכרו וילדו ב' זכרים ונתערבו זה נותן כו':
notes.en: Two wives: of two men, who had not given birth, and they bore two males and they were intermingled: this one gives, and so on.

messages.text: In a case where one of them dies within thirty days of birth, if the fathers gave all ten sela coins to one priest, the priest must return five sela coins to them.

notes.he: מן הוולדות יחזיר להם חמשה סלעים ויחלקו שני האבות:
notes.en: If one of them died: one of the newborns, [the priest] returns five sela to them, and the two fathers divide it.

messages.text: But if they gave the redemption payment to two different priests they cannot reclaim the money from the possession of either priest, as each could claim that the money that he received was for the living child.

notes.he: דכל חד וחד אומר אני מחזיק בם בשביל החי דאותו שנתן לי בשבילו לא מת וכל המוציא מחבירו ידו על התחתונה:
notes.en: And they cannot take it back: since each [priest] says, “I am holding it for the living one; the one it was given to me for did not die”; and whoever would take from his fellow has the weaker hand.

notes.he: דמצו למידחינהו דכל חד וחד אמר פדיון דחי תפיסנא:
notes.en: They cannot take it back from him: since [the priests] can put them off, for each one says, “I am holding the redemption of the living one.”

messages.text: If the women gave birth to a male and a female and the children became intermingled, the fathers are exempt, as each could claim that he is the father of the female, but the son is obligated to redeem himself, as he is certainly a firstborn.

notes.he: דכל חד וחד אמר ליה לכהן הנקבה שלי היא:
notes.en: The fathers are exempt: since each one says to the priest, “The female is mine.”

notes.he: דמכל מקום בכור הוא:
notes.en: And the son is obligated to redeem himself: since in any case he is a firstborn.

notes.he: האבות פטורין דכל חד מצי אמר נקבה דידי היא אבל הבן חייב לפדות עצמו:
notes.en: A male and a female, and they were intermingled: the fathers are exempt, since each can say, “The female is mine”; but the son is obligated to redeem himself.

messages.text: If two females and a male were born, or two females and two males, the priest has nothing here, as it is possible the female was born first to each mother.

notes.he: יש לומר האחת ילדה נקבה ושנית זכר ונקבה ויצתה נקבה תחלה הלכך אין כאן לכהן כלום דיש לומר המבכרת ילדה הנקבה ע"כ וכן ב' זכרים ושתי נקבות:
notes.en: Two females and a male: one can say that one [woman] bore a female and the other a male and a female, and the female came out first. Therefore the priest has nothing here, since one can say the first-time mother bore the female. [Rashi’s comment] ends here. And the same applies to two males and two females.

notes.he: דאחת ילדה זכר ונקבה ואחת נקבה או כל אחת זכר ונקבה:
notes.en: Two females and a male: where one bore a male and a female and one a female; or [two males and two females, where] each bore a male and a female.

messages.text: If one woman had previously given birth and one had not previously given birth, and they were married to two men and they gave birth to two males, who then became intermingled, this one whose wife had not previously given birth gives five sela coins to the priest.

notes.he: ונתערבו זה שלא ביכרה אשתו כיון דילדה זכר אע"ג דלא ידע הי ניהו נותן ה' סלעים לכהן:
notes.en: And they bore two males, and they were intermingled: this one whose wife had not given birth before, since she bore a male, even though one does not know which he is, gives five sela to the priest.

messages.text: If the women gave birth to a male and a female the priest has nothing here, as it is possible the female was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

notes.he: ונתערבו אין כאן לכהן כלום דשמא דההיא דביכרה ילדה נקבה:
notes.en: They bore a male and a female, and they were intermingled: the priest has nothing here, since perhaps the one bearing her firstborn bore the female.

messages.caption: The mishnayot’s cases at a glance: who bore what, and what the priest receives.

messages.text: Gemara

What is different about a case where the fathers gave the redemption money to two different priests, and one of the firstborns subsequently died, that they cannot reclaim the money? The reason is that one father will go to this priest and he will reject him, by claiming that he took the redemption money for the surviving firstborn, and likewise he will go to that other priest and he too will reject him in the same manner.
messages.quote: But if they gave the redemption payment to two different priests they cannot reclaim the money

notes.he: דאינו יכול להוציא מידם. מאי שנא כהן א' דמחזיר. כהן אחד נמי מצי מדחי כל חד וחד דמצי אמר לכל חד וחד דידך הוא:
notes.en: What is different about two priests, that he cannot take it back from them, and what is different about one priest, that he returns it? With one priest too, he can put off each one, for he can say to each one, “What I hold is yours [the redemption of your living son].”

messages.text: The same is also true in a case where they gave their redemption money to one priest: This father will go to the priest and the priest will reject him, by claiming that his son is still alive, and that father will go to the priest and he will reject him too, on the same grounds.

notes.he: ומב' אבות שקל כי אזיל לגביה האי אב לידחייה כהן ולימא לא שלך מת אלא של חבירך ולאו בעל דברים דידי את:
notes.en: Gemara. With one priest too: who took from two fathers; when this father goes to him, let the priest put him off and say, “It is not yours that died but your fellow’s, and you are not the one I have a case with.”

notes.he: בבא כל אחד בהרשאה ואמר ליה אי מת דידי הוא אהדר לי ואי דחבראי הא נקיטנא הרשאה מיניה. אבל לתרי כהנים לא מצי עבדי הרשאה. דלכל חד אמר אנא לית לי אלא ה' סלעים דחי:
notes.en: Shmuel said: where each comes with authorization [from the other] and says to him, “If the one who died is mine, give it back to me; and if it is my fellow’s, here, I hold his authorization.” But with two priests they cannot make use of authorization, since each [priest] says, “I have only five sela, those of the living one.”

messages.text: Shmuel says: … his answer continues on 49a: one father comes with authorization to claim on behalf of the other.
